slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 49:10: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.
slides.body: “The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.”
slides.heading: Gen 49:10

slides.body: Genesis 49:10 describes the allegiance of nations. John 10:16 describes other sheep hearing Jesus’s voice and becoming one flock under one shepherd. Christians connect these pictures of a people gathered under one ruler.
slides.heading: Nations and one flock

slides.body: Several readings of Genesis retain an international horizon, and early Jewish interpretation is messianic. Read as a gathering beyond Israel, Jesus’s other sheep fit the hope of peoples united under Judah’s promised ruler.
slides.heading: A coherent messianic reading

slides.body: John does not cite Genesis, and one listening flock is not identical to international political obedience. The connection supports a Christian theological reading but does not uniquely identify Jesus through a testable prediction.
slides.heading: A parallel with limits

title: Do Jesus’s “other sheep” fulfil the allegiance of the nations?
